text:
maria: Quick sync — we need to land a final convention for customer-facing audit event names (URN-ish) + action verbs before the RBAC rollout next week. thoughts?
aj: +1 — current mix of `user.login_success` and `auth.user_login` is messy. we should pick one pattern and stick to it.
sasha: Agree. Proposal: `com.redwood.<product>.<resource>.<action>` e.g. `com.redwood.inference.model.deploy` or `com.redwood.console.user.invite.send`.
vikram: That pattern looks good. Two questions: 1) verbs: should they be present tense `create`/`delete` or past `created`/`deleted`? 2) how do we express failing vs success? separate suffix or attribute?
lin: I'd keep verbs in imperative/present (`create`, `update`, `delete`, `deploy`) and encode outcome in `status` or `result` field (e.g., `result: success|failure|partial`). simpler for consumers parsing.
maria: +1 to present tense + `result` field. Also we should reserve a namespace for internal-only events: `internal.redwood.*` to avoid customer-facing leakage.
aj: For RBAC mapping we need stable resource nouns. e.g., `model`, `deployment`, `key` (for KMS), `policy`. Avoid plurals.
sasha: Good call. Also propose a short event versioning scheme on the event envelope: `event_version` and `schema_id` so we can evolve without breaking older consumers.
vikram: Ops: can we standardize `actor.type` values? right now we have `user`, `service`, `system`, `admin`. consumer teams rely on `user` vs `service` for alerting.
lin: yes — let's lock `actor.type` to that set and add `actor.id` and `actor.affiliated_org` optional.
maria: quick example for docs (feel free to tweak):
```
{
  "event_name": "com.redwood.inference.model.deploy",
  "event_version": "1",
  "occurred_at": "2026-03-19T22:12:34Z",
  "actor": {"type": "user", "id": "u-123", "email": "alice@example.com"},
  "resource": {"type": "model", "id": "m-abc"},
  "action": "deploy",
  "result": "success",
  "metadata": {"region": "us-west-2", "deployment_size": "g4dn.xlarge"}
}
```
aj: nice. One more: KMS-related events should include `kms_key_id` and a `sensitivity` tag so compliance can filter.
sasha: Also call out PII — don't put PII in top-level `metadata` fields if events are routed to external sinks. We should add `redaction_policy` field and default to `mask_emails` for customer-facing streams.
vikram: For rollout: create a lint rule in `event-spec` repo to enforce naming regex: `^com\.redwood\.[a-z0-9_]+\.[a-z0-9_]+\.[a-z0-9_]+$` and check `actor.type` set. That will catch odd names.
lin: +1. Who owns the naming registry? we need a single source of truth.
maria: Security owns the registry but will accept PRs from product/ingest teams. process: open PR in `event-spec`, get two approvals (sec + owning product), CI lint passes, then we tag `schema_id` and publish to docs.
aj: timeline: can we freeze customer-facing names by EOD Thursday? RBAC changes ship Friday.
sasha: I'll batch current proposals and open PR by Wednesday.
audit-bot: Note: There are 5 unregistered event names referenced in `eng-platform` open PRs. See <https://git.internal.redwood/event-spec/pending> :eyes:
vikram: ok thanks bot. action items:
- sasha: PR w/ proposed names by Wed
- aj: add lint rule + CI check by Thurs morning
- lin: update RBAC mapping doc to reference new nouns
- maria: publish namespace + registry process doc
lin: I'll update the RBAC CSV with new resource names and ping integrators.
aj: I'll draft the regex and add a test harness for converting legacy names to new URNs (for backward compat).
maria: cool. if nobody objects, I'll announce the registry and process in #eng-platform and ping PMs. :thumbsup:
sasha: no objections from me.
vikram: one last thought — include a `compatibility` field when we deprecate names to help downstream consumers transition.
maria: good point. add `deprecated_by` and `deprecated_at` to the registry entries.
lin: ack.
maria: thanks all — follow-ups on PRs. closing thread.
